_about: Deliberately small starter vocabulary for how an organization works. Use this when no other ontology fits. A FIRST DRAFT to edit.
_summary: How an organization works: units, roles, processes, policies, systems and measures.
name: Operations Knowledge Base

classes.Unit: An organizational unit: a division, a department, a team.
classes.Role: A defined function someone performs. Attach work to a role, not a person.
classes.Process: A repeatable way of getting something done, made of steps.
classes.Step: One action within a process, with an owner and an input and output.
classes.Policy: A rule that constrains how work is done, internal or imposed.
classes.System: A tool or application the work runs on.
classes.Measure: Something the organization tracks to know whether the work is working.
classes.Decision: A choice made, with its reason and date. Superseded by a later one, never overwritten.
classes.Document: A source document in the corpus.

part_of: A containment relationship: a unit within a unit, a step within a process.
performs: The role that carries out a step.
belongs_to: The unit a role sits in.
uses: A system the work depends on.
supersedes: This replaced that. Use with the temporal fields, never by overwriting.
